noGrub.title: This system does not boot with GRUB
noGrub.body: The file /etc/default/grub or the update-grub command was not found, so there is nothing to edit here. Nothing has been changed.

backup.title: Save a copy first?
backup.body: Before the first change, you can save a copy of /etc/default/grub wherever you want. You will not be asked again until the program is restarted.
backup.saveTitle: Save a copy of the GRUB settings

pending.discardBody: The changes that have not been applied yet will be lost.

job.running: Working on it. Do not close the program; this can take a minute.
job.done: Done. GRUB was updated and the changes will be there at the next boot.
job.failed: A step failed and the rest were not made. Some changes may already be in place: review them before trying again, or discard the list.

general.bootConfigSub: What starts by default and for how long the menu waits.
general.modeFixedText: Always starts the entry you choose below.
general.modeLastInstalledText: Starts the first entry of the menu, normally the newest kernel.
general.modeLastBootedText: Starts whatever you started last time.
general.advancedSub: What the menu detects and shows.
general.menuNeedsTimeout: The menu cannot be shown when the timeout is 0
general.uuid: Use the UUID of the root partition
general.kernelParamsSub: Options passed to the kernel at every boot.

entries.empty: There are no boot entries to show.
entries.unreadable: The boot menu (grub.cfg) can only be read with administrator rights on this system.
entries.addHint: Write the GRUB menuentry block. It is added to /etc/grub.d/40_custom after GRUB checks it.
entries.removeMemtest: Delete {name} from /boot? This also removes its serial-console variant, since both use the same file.
entries.removeCustom: Delete {name} from /etc/grub.d/40_custom? This cannot be undone.
entries.notSupported: This entry belongs to an installed kernel or operating system. GRUB generates it from what is installed on the disk, so it cannot be switched off or removed one by one here: you would have to uninstall the kernel or the operating system itself.

appearance.emptyThemesBody: Install a theme from an archive (.zip, .tar.gz...) and it will show up here.
appearance.themeInfo: A theme includes its own colors and fonts. For your own image and colors, use the Background tab.
appearance.installFailed: The theme could not be installed.
appearance.applyThemeBody: Applying {name} turns off any custom background and colors. Continue?
appearance.disableThemeBody: This removes the theme and goes back to plain colors. Continue?
appearance.removeThemeBody: This permanently deletes the theme {name}. Are you sure?
appearance.colorsInfo: Colors, when no theme is used.
appearance.applyLookBody: This turns off any theme and uses your background and colors. Continue?
appearance.removeBackgroundBody: This removes the background image from GRUB. The colors stay. Continue?
appearance.convertInfo: Convert a TrueType or OpenType font to GRUB's format (PF2).
appearance.convertFailed: The font could not be converted.
appearance.removeFontBody: This permanently deletes the font {name}. Are you sure?

hints.bootMode: Fixed entry always starts the same entry. Last installed kernel starts the first entry of the menu. Last booted kernel starts whatever was started last time.
hints.bootEntry: Only used with a fixed entry. In the other two modes GRUB chooses by itself.
hints.timeout: Seconds the menu waits before it starts the default entry. With 0 it starts at once.
hints.resolution: Resolution of the boot menu. Auto lets GRUB choose the one of your screen.
hints.detectOs: Looks for other operating systems on your disks and adds them to the menu. It needs the os-prober package.
hints.showMenu: When off, the menu stays hidden and the default entry starts unless you hold the Shift key.
hints.recovery: Adds a recovery mode entry for each kernel, to repair the system when it does not start.
hints.uuid: Identifies the root partition by its UUID instead of its device name, which can change when disks are added.
hints.submenu: Without submenus, every kernel is listed in the main menu instead of inside Advanced options.
hints.kernelParams: Separated by spaces. Quiet and splash hide the boot messages. Change them with care: a wrong option can stop the system from starting.
hints.entriesIntro: Each row is an entry of the boot menu. The switch turns an entry off or on without deleting it.
hints.entriesToggle: Only memtest and your own entries can be changed. Kernel entries follow what is installed. Changes wait in the bar at the bottom until you apply them all.
hints.themeChoice: Install a theme from an archive, choose it and add it to the changes. Disable returns to plain colors. Nothing is written until you press Apply all.
hints.backgroundImage: A PNG or JPEG image. It is shown behind the menu when no theme is applied.
hints.colors: GRUB can only show sixteen colors, so the choice is limited to them.
hints.fontConvert: GRUB cannot read normal fonts. This converts a TTF or OTF file and keeps it in /boot/grub/fonts.
hints.fontApply: Adding it to the changes sets this font for the menu once you apply them. Removing a font in use also clears the setting.

general.what: Sets how the boot menu behaves: which entry starts by default, how long the menu waits, the screen resolution, what it detects and the parameters passed to the kernel.
general.care: The default entry is only written when you choose it, so opening this page and applying never pins the boot to the current kernel. A wrong kernel parameter can stop the system from starting.

entries.what: Lists the entries of the boot menu. The memtest entries and the ones you add can be switched off and on or deleted. New entries are checked by GRUB before they are saved.
entries.care: Kernel and operating system entries are generated from what is installed, so they cannot be changed one by one. Deleting memtest deletes its file from /boot.

appearance.what: Changes how the boot menu looks: an installed theme, or your own background and colors, and the font. A theme and a custom look exclude each other, so applying one clears the other.
appearance.care: Themes come as archives and are unpacked in a private folder before they are installed. Applying a look turns off the scripts that add a theme of their own.
